reading_decisions.why: Its two codes match the corpus exactly: corrections coincide with user revisions (E04, E08, E12) and tool failures terminate uncorrected (E02, E06, E10), and its stated limit about absent self-correction loops is accurate.

The split of target redirection from design reversal is a useful refinement, but 'misidentifies the target' overstates E08 and E12, which read as changed preferences rather than corrected mistakes, and like the others it ignores the unknown-status episodes.
Its three-code split is the most granular and every quote and status checks out; its shared blind spot on E03/E07/E11 is an extension opportunity, not an error.

output.what_changed_my_view: The three readings converged on the same correction episodes (E04, E08, E12), which matched my own read, so they mostly confirmed rather than changed my view. The divergence view's uncited-episode list (E03, E07, E11) pushed me to add the unknown-status pattern and the E07 conditional-commit open question, which no reading covered.
